a1.say: Let's solve Search a Fully Sorted Grid, using the Binary Search as One List approach.

card.title: Search a Fully Sorted Grid
card.sub: Binary Search as One List · Medium

a1.cap: In the m × n grid grid, each row is sorted left to right and each row's first value is greater than the previous row's last value. Return true if target is in the grid, in O(log(m·n)).
a1.say: In the m times n grid grid, each row is sorted left to right and each row's first value is greater than the previous row's last value. Return true if target is in the grid, in O of log(m times n).

lines: In the m × n grid grid, each row is sorted left to right and each row's first value is greater than the previous row's last value. Return true if target is in the grid, in O(log(m·n)).

a1.cap: For example, with grid = [[1,3,5,7],[10,11,16,20],[23,30,34,60]], target = 3, the answer is true.
a1.say: For example, with grid equals 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 16, 20, 23, 30, 34, 60, target equals 3, the answer is true.

a1.cap: Read row by row, the grid is one long sorted list of m·n values. Binary search positions 0 to m·n − 1 and convert each position into a row and column.
a1.say: Read row by row, the grid is one long sorted list of m times n values. Binary search positions 0 to m times n minus 1 and convert each position into a row and column.
